title: Consumer Relationship Exposure Rule for Kestrel Advantage Balloon Bookings
content:
Kestrel limits the total consumer credit it extends to one customer across products. For a Kestrel Advantage Balloon Retail Installment Sale Contract being booked or funded, relationship exposure must not exceed the relationship exposure cap of the tier being booked.

## Definition of relationship exposure

Relationship exposure is the total of:

1. the principal balance on every open retail, pre-owned and balloon contract of the customer;
2. the adjusted lease balance on every lease of the customer in active or maturity-extended status;
3. the amount financed of the contract being booked.

Business customers' fleet units are commercial credit and never count toward consumer relationship exposure.

## Decision

| Relationship exposure compared with the tier's cap | Result |
|---|---|
| At or below the cap | The cap does not stand in the way of funding |
| Above the cap | The contract is not funded |

There is no partial approval and no override at the servicing desk. The test is made on the company's own records of the customer's contracts and leases, matched to the customer of the contract being booked, before the booking or funding takes place. The cap for each tier is the relationship exposure cap in the tier's underwriting schedule.

## Worked case (hypothetical figures)

A customer is booking a balloon contract of USD 20000.00 on a tier whose cap is USD 60000.00. The customer has an open retail contract with principal of USD 15000.00 and an active lease with an adjusted lease balance of USD 22000.00. Exposure is USD 57000.00, at or below the cap. Had the lease been in a status other than active or maturity-extended, its balance would not have entered the total.
